paras.en: The fourth planet belonged to the businessman. This man was so busy that he did not even raise his head when the little prince arrived.
paras.zh: 第四颗星球是商人的星球。这个人忙得连小王子来了都没有抬一下头。

paras.en: “Hello,” the little prince said to him. “Your cigarette has gone out.”
paras.zh: “你好，”小王子对他说，“你的香烟灭了。”

paras.en: “Three and two make five. Five and seven, twelve. Twelve and three, fifteen. Hello. Fifteen and seven, twenty-two. Twenty-two and six, twenty-eight. No time to light it again. Twenty-six and five, thirty-one. Phew! So that makes five hundred and one million, six hundred and twenty-two thousand, seven hundred and thirty-one.”
paras.zh: “三加二等于五。五加七，十二。十二加三，十五。你好。十五加七，二十二。二十二加六，二十八。没时间重新点了。二十六加五，三十一。呼！这么说，一共是五亿一百六十二万二千七百三十一。”

paras.en: “Five hundred million what?”
paras.zh: “五亿什么？”

paras.en: “Eh? Are you still here? Five hundred and one million… I can't remember what… I have so much work to do! I'm serious, I don't amuse myself with nonsense! Two and five, seven…”
paras.zh: “嗯？你还在这儿？五亿一百万……什么来着……我有这么多工作要做！我可是个认真的人，不拿无聊的事消遣！二加五，七……”

paras.en: “Five hundred million what?” repeated the little prince, who had never in his life given up on a question once he had asked it.
paras.zh: “五亿什么？”小王子又问了一遍。他这辈子只要问出了一个问题，就从来不肯放下。

paras.en: The businessman raised his head:
paras.zh: 商人抬起头来：

paras.en: “In the fifty-four years I've lived on this planet, I've been disturbed only three times. The first time was twenty-two years ago, by a cockchafer that had fallen from God knows where. It made a dreadful noise, and I made four mistakes in one addition. The second time was eleven years ago, by an attack of rheumatism. I don't get enough exercise. I have no time to stroll about. I'm serious. The third time… here it is! So, I was saying, five hundred and one million…”
paras.zh: “我在这颗星球上住了五十四年，只被打扰过三次。第一次是二十二年前，一只金龟子，天知道从哪里掉下来的。它发出可怕的响声，害我一道加法算错了四处。第二次是十一年前，风湿病发作。我缺少运动。我没时间闲逛。我可是个认真的人。第三次……就是现在！我刚才说到五亿一百万……”

paras.en: “Millions of what?”
paras.zh: “你说的百万，是百万个什么？”

paras.en: The businessman realised there was no hope of peace:
paras.zh: 商人明白，想要清静是没有指望了：

paras.en: “Millions of those little things you sometimes see in the sky.”
paras.zh: “成百万的那种有时在天上能看见的小东西。”

paras.en: “Flies?”
paras.zh: “苍蝇？”

paras.en: “Of course not, little things that shine.”
paras.zh: “当然不是，是会发光的小东西。”

paras.en: “Bees?”
paras.zh: “蜜蜂？”

paras.en: “Of course not. Little golden things that make lazy people daydream. But I’m serious, I am! I have no time to daydream.”
paras.zh: “当然不是。是金色的小东西，会让懒人做白日梦。可我是个认真的人！我没有时间做白日梦。”

paras.en: “Ah! Stars?”
paras.zh: “啊！星星？”

paras.en: “That’s right. Stars.”
paras.zh: “没错。星星。”

paras.en: “And what do you do with the five hundred million stars?”
paras.zh: “那你拿这五亿颗星星做什么呢？”

paras.en: “Five hundred and one million, six hundred and twenty-two thousand, seven hundred and thirty-one. I’m a serious man, I am. I’m precise.”
paras.zh: “五亿零一百六十二万二千七百三十一。我可是个认真的人，我讲究精确。”

paras.en: “And what do you do with those stars?”
paras.zh: “那你拿这些星星做什么呢？”

paras.en: “What do I do with them?”
paras.zh: “我拿它们做什么？”

paras.en: “Yes.”
“Nothing. I own them.”
paras.zh: “什么也不做。我拥有它们。”

paras.en: “You own the stars?”
paras.zh: “你拥有星星？”

paras.en: “Yes.”
“But I’ve already seen a king who…”
paras.zh: “可是我已经见过一位国王，他……”

paras.en: “Kings don’t own them. They ‘rule’ over them. That’s very different.”
paras.zh: “国王并不拥有它们。他们‘统治’它们。这很不一样。”

paras.en: “And what use is it to you to own the stars?”
paras.zh: “那拥有星星对你有什么用呢？”

paras.en: “It makes me rich.”
paras.zh: “能让我有钱。”

paras.en: “And what use is it to you to be rich?”
paras.zh: “那有钱对你有什么用呢？”

paras.en: “To buy more stars, if anyone finds any.”
paras.zh: “用来买别的星星，要是有人找到的话。”

paras.en: This one, the little prince thought to himself, reasons a little like my drunkard.
paras.zh: 这个人，小王子心想，他讲起道理来，有点像我那个酒鬼。

paras.en: Still, he went on asking questions:
paras.zh: 不过，他还是接着问了下去：

paras.en: “How can anyone own the stars?”
paras.zh: “一个人怎么能拥有星星呢？”

paras.en: “Who do they belong to?” the businessman shot back grumpily.
paras.zh: “那它们是谁的？”商人没好气地反问。

paras.en: “I don’t know. No one.”
paras.zh: “我不知道。谁的也不是。”

paras.en: “Then they belong to me, because I thought of it first.”
paras.zh: “那它们就是我的，因为是我第一个想到的。”

paras.en: “Is that enough?”
paras.zh: “这样就够了吗？”

paras.en: “Of course. When you find a diamond that belongs to no one, it is yours. When you find an island that belongs to no one, it is yours. When you are the first to have an idea, you take out a patent on it: it is yours. And I own the stars, since no one before me ever thought of owning them.”
paras.zh: “当然。你找到一颗不属于任何人的钻石，它就是你的。你找到一座不属于任何人的岛，它就是你的。你第一个想到一个主意，就把它注册成专利：它就是你的。而我拥有星星，因为在我之前，从来没有人想过要拥有它们。”

paras.en: “That’s true,” said the little prince. “And what do you do with them?”
paras.zh: “这倒是真的，”小王子说，“那你拿它们做什么呢？”

paras.en: “I manage them. I count them and I count them again,” said the businessman. “It’s difficult. But I am a serious man!”
paras.zh: “我管理它们。我数它们，数了又数，”商人说，“这很难。不过，我是个认真的人！”

paras.en: The little prince was still not satisfied.
paras.zh: 小王子还是不满意。

paras.en: “As for me, if I own a scarf, I can put it round my neck and take it with me. As for me, if I own a flower, I can pick my flower and take it with me. But you can’t pick the stars!”
paras.zh: “我呢，如果有一条围巾，就可以把它围在脖子上，带着走。我呢，如果有一朵花，就可以摘下我的花，带着走。可你不能把星星摘下来呀！”

paras.en: “No, but I can put them in the bank.”
paras.zh: “不能，不过我可以把它们存进银行。”

paras.en: “What does that mean?”
paras.zh: “那是什么意思？”

paras.en: “It means I write down the number of my stars on a little piece of paper. And then I lock that piece of paper in a drawer.”
paras.zh: “意思就是，我把我的星星的数目写在一张小纸片上。然后把那张纸片锁在抽屉里。”

paras.en: “And that’s all?”
paras.zh: “就这样吗？”

paras.en: “That’s enough!”
paras.zh: “这样就够了！”

paras.en: That’s amusing, thought the little prince. It’s quite poetic. But it isn’t very serious.
paras.zh: 这挺有趣，小王子想。还挺有诗意。不过不怎么认真。

paras.en: The little prince’s ideas about serious things were very different from the ideas of grown-ups.
paras.zh: 对于正经事，小王子的想法和大人们的想法很不一样。

paras.en: “As for me,” he went on, “I own a flower that I water every day. I own three volcanoes that I sweep out every week. Because I sweep out the extinct one too. You never know. My owning them is useful to my volcanoes, and it is useful to my flower. But you are no use to the stars...”
paras.zh: “我呢，”他又说，“我拥有一朵花，每天都给它浇水。我拥有三座火山，每个星期都给它们清理烟灰。因为连那座熄灭的火山，我也清理。谁也说不准。我拥有它们，这对我的火山有用，对我的花也有用。可是你对星星没有用……”

paras.en: The businessman opened his mouth but could find no reply, and the little prince went away.
paras.zh: 商人张开嘴，却想不出什么话来回答，小王子便离开了。

paras.en: Grown-ups really are quite extraordinary, he simply said to himself as he travelled.
paras.zh: 大人们实在是太奇怪了，他在旅途中只是这样对自己说。
